{{short description|Gives a functional equation satisfied by the generating function of any rational cone}}
'''Stanley's reciprocity theorem''', named after the mathematician [[Richard P. Stanley]], states that a certain [[functional equation]] is satisfied by the integer-point [[generating function]] of a rational cone and the generating function of the cone's interior.

== Definitions ==
A '''rational cone''' is a subset of <math>{\bf R}^d</math> consisting of all points satisfying a finite set of homogeneous linear inequalities with integer coefficients or, alternatively, the nonnegative span of a finite set of integer vectors. That is, a rational cone {{math|''C''}} has the two alternative descriptions

:<math>C = \left\{ x \in {\bf R}^d : Ax \le 0 \right\}</math>

for some <math>m \times d</math> integer matrix {{math|''A''}} (i.e., {{math|''C''}} is defined by the {{math|''m''}} halfspaces given by the rows of {{math|''A''}}), and

:<math>C = \left\{ By : y \ge 0 \right\}</math>

for some <math>d \times n</math> integer matrix {{math|''B''}} (i.e., {{math|''C''}} is defined as the nonnegative span of the {{math|''n''}} columns of {{math|''B''}}).

The '''integer-point generating function''' (also called <i>integer-point transform</i>) of such a cone {{math|''C''}} is

:<math>F_C(x_1,\dots,x_d)=\sum_{(a_1,\dots,a_d)\in C \cap {\bf Z}^d} x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_d^{a_d}.</math>

The generating function <math>F_{{\rm int}(C)}(x_1,\dots,x_d)</math> of the interior of the cone is defined analogously.
It can be shown that these generating functions evaluate to [[rational function]]s.

== The Reciprocity Theorem ==
Stanley's reciprocity theorem states that for a <math>d</math>-dimensional rational cone <math>C</math>, we have the following identity of rational functions:<ref>{{cite journal |first=Richard P. |last=Stanley |title=Combinatorial reciprocity theorems |journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]] |volume=14 |issue=2 |pages=194–253 |year=1974 |doi=10.1016/0001-8708(74)90030-9 |doi-access=free |url=http://math.mit.edu/~rstan/pubs/pubfiles/22.pdf}}</ref>

:<math>F_C(1/x_1,\dots,1/x_d)=(-1)^d F_{{\rm int}(C)}(x_1,\dots,x_d).</math>

Stanley's reciprocity theorem generalizes Ehrhart-Macdonald reciprocity for [[Ehrhart polynomials]] of rational [[Convex polytope|convex polytopes]]. Both of these results are examples of <i>combinatorial reciprocity theorems</i>,<ref name=becksanyal>{{citation
 | last1 = Beck | first1 = Matthias
 | last2 = Sanyal | first2 = Raman
 | isbn = 978-1-4704-2200-4
 | publisher = American Mathematical Society
 | series = [[Graduate Studies in Mathematics]]
 | title = Combinatorial Reciprocity Theorems: An Invitation to Enumerative Geometric Combinatorics
 | year = 2018}}</ref>
a term that was, in fact, also coined by Stanley.
